Research note: every network tool in this session (websearch, webfetch, bash/curl, computer) is returning "permission required but no prompt available," so I could not hit britishmuseum.org or the Science Advances page directly. I cross-checked what was available locally (prior session logs in `.goathome/sessions` show the same blocked state, no cached page text), and relied on established knowledge:

- British Museum museum number 2012,5015.17 is a shell of the triton/nassariid *Tritia gibbosula* (= *Nassarius gibbosulus*), the species used for prehistoric marine shell beads in North Africa.
- The 2021 *Science Advances* article on such beads is Kuhn et al., "142,000-year-old triton shell beads from Bizmoune Cave, Morocco" (Sci. Adv. 7(37), 2021), whose abstract states the beads date to at least 142,000 years ago — roughly 32,000 years older than the next oldest known beads.

Per the question's "thousands of years" phrasing, the number sought is 142. If you want a live re-verification once network access is enabled, check:
- https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/P_2012,5015.17
- https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abi5960

ANSWER: 142
